newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-May 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-May 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- Academics criticised the Chief Executive's Office's proposal to amend two civil rights ordinances, pointing out that there were many flaws which needed to be improved.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The 15th General Conference of the Chinese Communist Party would be held in September, two months earlier than scheduled, and the Party's Central Committee would be re-structured to strengthen President Jiang Zemin's position.

-- APPLE DAILY -- A poll showed 65 percent of Hong Kong people trusted the Hong Kong government, while only 30 percent had confidence in the Chinese government. It also showed few people were excited about the handover.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen met U.S. President Bill Clinton and refuted the "China Threat" theory. Qian also assured Clinton that Hong Kong people would enjoy more freedom after the handover.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Wharf (Holdings) was ordered by a U.S. court to pay a U.S. cable television company US$125.5 million after being judged guilty of fraud, breach of promise and deceit.

-- Proposals on amending Hong Kong's company and securities law will be announced by the government, including significant changes in directors' accountability to shareholders and radical reform of the capital structure of companies.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Cathay Pacific will consider increasing its U.S. destinations to include Chicago should fees at Chek Lap Kok airport prove reasonable.
-- Washington sources said the United States had decided to treat the Provisional Legislative Council as an "illegitimate body" and would not recognise it even after the handover.
